prompt_context: Draft an Application for Cancellation of Bail under BNSS Section 483(3) (High Court / Sessions Court) read with BNSS Section 480. The petitioner may be the State, informant, or even the accused (in case of seeking variation of onerous conditions imposed). Cancellation grounds are well-established (Dolat Ram v. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349; Bhagirathsinh v. State of Gujarat (1984) 1 SCC 284): (1) tampering with evidence; (2) threatening or influencing witnesses; (3) breach of bail conditions; (4) commission of similar/fresh offence while on bail; (5) abuse of concession; (6) fleeing from justice. The court that granted bail (or a superior court) has jurisdiction to cancel. The application must distinguish between 'cancellation' (for misconduct post-bail) and 'setting aside' (for being granted on irrelevant considerations). Reference BNS section numbers throughout — never IPC.
promptInstructions: Draft an Application for Cancellation of Bail under Section 483(3) BNSS, 2023 read with Section 480 BNSS.
If party_role = 'State / Prosecution' or 'Informant', frame as cancellation due to misconduct or breach by accused.
If party_role = 'Accused', frame as application for variation/relaxation of bail conditions (NOT cancellation of own bail).
Set out the bail order particulars: date, application number, conditions imposed, granting court.
State supervening events that justify cancellation — be specific with dates, places, witness names where possible.
Cite Dolat Ram v. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349 and Bhagirathsinh v. State of Gujarat (1984) 1 SCC 284 on grounds for cancellation.
Use BNS sections for underlying offences (never IPC).
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
